text: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt, marrying his daughter and bringing her to the city of David until his palace, the LORD's house, and Jerusalem's wall were finished.
The people were still sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the LORD's name.
Solomon loved the LORD and walked in his father David's statutes, except that he too sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, Ask what I should give you.

Solomon answered, You showed great steadfast love to my father David, who walked before you in faithfulness and righteousness, and you kept this great love for him by giving him a son to sit on his throne this day.
And now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, but I am only a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.
Your servant is among the people you have chosen, a great people, too many to count or number.
So give your servant an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil, for who is able to govern this great people of yours?
It pleased the LORD that Solomon had asked this.
God said to him, Because you asked this, and not for long life or riches or the life of your enemies, but for understanding to discern what is right,
I now do according to your word; I give you a wise and discerning mind, so that none before you has been like you, nor shall any after you arise like you.
I also give you what you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that no other king shall compare with you all your days.
And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commandments as your father David walked, I will lengthen your days.
Solomon awoke, and it had been a dream; he came to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
One woman said, Oh my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth to a child while she was in the house.
On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth; we were together, no stranger with us in the house, only the two of us.
This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.
She arose at midnight and took my son from beside me while your servant slept, and laid him at her breast, and laid her dead son at my breast.
When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, he was dead; but when I looked closely in the morning, it was not the son I had borne.
The other woman said, No, the living son is mine, and the dead son is yours. But the first said, No, the dead son is yours, and the living son is mine. So they argued before the king.
Then the king said, One says, This is my son who is alive, and your son is dead; and the other says, No, your son is dead, and my son is alive.
The king said, Bring me a sword. So they brought a sword before the king.
The king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one and half to the other.

Then the woman whose son was alive said to the king, for compassion for her son burned within her, Oh my lord, give her the living child, and do not put him to death. But the other said, He shall be neither mine nor yours; divide him.
Then the king answered, Give the living child to the first woman, and by no means put him to death; she is his mother.
All Israel heard of the judgment the king had rendered, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to do justice.
